quote: In this paper, we study this challenging area of automatic summarization of multiple alternative narratives from different perspectives.
We frame Semantic Overlap Summarization (SOS) … as a constrained multi-seq-to-seq (text generation) task where the output text only contains information that is present in both the input documents.

we frame the SOS task as a constrained seq-to-seq problem where the goal is to generate a summary from two input documents that convey the overlapping information present in both input text documents.
datasets: AllSides benchmark (137 narrative pairs, 548 reference summaries)
outputs: Generated summaries conveying common information from multiple input narratives
Overlap summaries containing only the common information from the two input narratives
overlap summary that conveys the common/overlapping information from multiple narratives

quote: As ROUGE is the most popular metric used today for evaluating summarization tasks; we first conducted a case study with ROUGE as the evaluation metric for the SOS task.

we propose a new precision-recall style evaluation metric, SEM-F 1 (Semantic F 1 ), for evaluating the SOS task.

we engaged human volunteers to thoroughly annotate the testing samples (narrative pairs) in order to create multiple reference overlap summaries for each pair.
guideline: if the human feels there is more than 75% overlap (between each system-generated sentence and any reference-summary sentence), assign label P, else if the human feels there is less than 25% overlap, assign label A, and else, assign PP otherwise.
Annotators assign overlap labels (P, PP, A) based on perceived percentage overlap with reference summaries.
